subject: The patch is named as the deliverable, never defined, and would drop half the work if produced
recordedOccasion: after the owner asked why six revisions were written straight into the checkout.
severity: F1 is high -- the rule was missed across six revisions by a session that had read it. F3 is high and independent: following the rule literally produces a patch that silently omits every new file.
scope: session management. The fix is a defined artifact, a named actor, and a guard.
read: git status and git diff --name-only over Revision 231's change set

findings.statement: A session composed correctly and then copied into the checkout six times, and never once produced a patch
Section 6 names the patch as the deliverable and never says how to produce one, where it goes, or who applies it
findings.sectionHeading: F2 -- the deliverable has no definition

resolution.whatWasDone: section 6 gained "A patch is a file, and this is how it is made", naming git add -N ., git diff > "$PATCH_DIR/<revision>-<slug>.patch" and $PATCH_DIR; section 0 step 6 named the actor

findings.statement: git diff in a session copy omits every untracked file, so the prescribed patch would have carried 9 of 14 paths
findings.sectionHeading: F3 -- the prescribed patch would have dropped five of fourteen paths

resolution.whatWasDone: the same bullet added "git add -N is not optional and its absence is silent", with the 9-of-14 measurement and the instruction to read the patch's file list against the change set

findings.statement: Nothing detects a write into the owner's checkout, and the signal that used to exist was removed by 0038
An index write leaves no trace in the working tree, so the tree comparison this bundle prescribes cannot see it
findings.sectionHeading: F5 — an index write is invisible to the verification this bundle prescribes

findings.statement: The phrase that authorizes an apply has two definitions, the broader is in the copy, and neither has a precondition on the checkout
findings.sectionHeading: F6 — two definitions of the ask, and no precondition on either

resolution.whatWasDone: §0 step 6 rewritten: the ask names a delivered artifact, do it retired, applying is a response never an initiation, the checkout must be git status --porcelain empty before applying and the index empty after; the conformant prompt brought onto it

decisions.decision: Section 6 now defines the patch — how, where and by whom — so F2 is closed by Revision 232 rather than by anything decided here
decisions.sectionHeading: D1 — the patch is defined, at Revision 232

decisions.decision: `git add -N` is the whole of F3's fix and Revision 232 recorded it, with F3's own measurement quoted
decisions.sectionHeading: D2 — `git add -N`, and F3's measurement is in the fix

decisions.decision: F1 needs no remedy of its own. It reports behaviour, and the thing that would have stopped it is F4's guard
decisions.sectionHeading: D3 — F1 is behaviour, and closes with the guard

decisions.decision: The guard is extended to the tool a bridged session actually writes through, and derives its protected root from the connected folder rather than CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR. Warn, never deny, on a shell call; deny only on a file commit
decisions.sectionHeading: D4 — the guard does not cover the tool this session writes through

decisions.decision: The remainder of F4 is not worked here. It is a toolkit write with no bundle type yet, and it is parked as 0050
decisions.sectionHeading: D5 — the remainder is parked, not worked

decisions.decision: The apply procedure gains one assertion: after applying, git diff --cached --name-only in the checkout must be empty
decisions.sectionHeading: D6 — assert the index is empty, because the tree comparison cannot

decisions.decision: The authorizing phrase is the source's and do it is retired. Applying is a response to a delivered patch, never an initiation; where an instruction could be either, the session composes and asks
decisions.sectionHeading: D7 — the ask names a delivered artifact, and never a task

decisions.decision: A session asserts the checkout is clean before applying and refuses otherwise, naming what is already there
decisions.sectionHeading: D8 — the checkout must be clean, and this is the coordinator's lock

edges.why: the rule cannot be followed until the artifact it names is defined
how a patch is produced and what it must carry are one answer
a patch that under-applies and a revision that ships a rendering defect are the same class: the tool exits 0 and the defect is downstream

indexNotes: A session's account of its own failure. Offered to be checked, not believed
